classification.difficultyReason: Read the two box plots, calculate spread measures, and organise a comparison of location, variability and negative skewness using the requested categories.

content.prompt: The test results in English and Mathematics for a class were recorded and displayed in the box-and-whisker plots.

spec.description: Unshaded horizontal box plots, English above Mathematics, with subject labels and a shared horizontal scale labelled from 0 to 100 in steps of 10. Source grey strokes become ordinary black house-style strokes.
spec.mathematics: English five-number summary: 10, 50, 70, 80, 95. Mathematics five-number summary: 50, 65, 75, 80, 90.
spec.answerVisibility: All plots, subject labels and axis ticks are permanent student-visible givens; no answers are drawn.

children.prompt: What is the interquartile range for English?

children.label: b
children.prompt: Compare and contrast the two data sets by referring to the skewness of the distributions and the measures of location and spread.

answer.short: Both distributions are negatively skewed. Mathematics has a higher median ($75$ versus $70$) and minimum ($50$ versus $10$). English has a larger range ($85$ versus $40$) and IQR ($30$ versus $15$), so its results are more spread out.
answer.worked:
Skewness: Both distributions are negatively skewed: their left whiskers are longer and their medians are closer to the upper quartiles.

Location: Mathematics has a higher median ($75$) than English ($70$). Its minimum ($50$) is also higher than English's minimum ($10$).

Spread: English has range $95-10=85$, compared with $90-50=40$ for Mathematics. English has IQR $80-50=30$, compared with $80-65=15$ for Mathematics. Thus both the overall results and the middle $50\%$ of results are more spread out in English.
